info.title: Cisco Meraki Dashboard API — devices
info.description: The devices operations of the Cisco Meraki Dashboard API, split by product area from Cisco's published OpenAPI definition.

x-provenance.note: Split by first tag from Cisco's published spec3.json; operations unmodified.

get.description: Return the SIM and APN configurations for a cellular device.

slot.description: SIM slot being configured. Must be 'sim1' on single-sim devices. eSIM slots use the raw slot value for the device, such as 'sim2' or 'sim3'.

msisdn.description: Mobile Station Integrated Services Digital Network

isPrimary.description: If true, this SIM is activated on platform bootup. It must be true on single-SIM devices and is a required field for dual-SIM MGs unless it is being configured using 'simOrdering'.

status.description: Status of the SIM card.

allowedIpTypes.description: IP versions to support (permitted values include 'ipv4', 'ipv6').

username.description: APN username, if type is set.

password.description: APN password, if type is set (if APN password is not supplied, the password is left unchanged).

apns.description: APN configurations. If empty, the default APN will be used.

sims.description: List of SIMs. If a SIM was previously configured and not specified in this request, it will remain unchanged.

simOrdering.description: Specifies the ordering of all SIMs for an MG: primary, secondary, and not-in-use (when applicable). It's required for devices with 3 or more SIMs and can be used in place of 'isPrimary' for dual-SIM devices. Use the raw eSIM slot value for the device, such as 'sim2' or 'sim3'. Sim failover will occur only between primary and secondary sim slots.

post.description: Update the cellular band masks for a device

slot.description: Required parameter for the SIM slot to update the cellular band mask for

type.description: Required parameter for the signal type to update the cellular band mask for

masked.description: Required parameter for the band identifiers to mask for the given SIM slot and signal type. For LTE use bands identifiers like '30', for 5G use band identifiers like 'n30', or use 'all' to mask all bands for that signal type. Maximum 256 bands.
List of masked band identifiers. For LTE use bands identifiers like '30', for 5G use band identifiers like 'n30', or 'all' when all bands are masked. Maximum 256 bands per signal type.

enabled.description: List of enabled band identifiers.  For LTE use bands identifiers like '30' and for 5G use band identifiers like 'n30'. Maximum 256 bands per signal type.

supported.description: List of supported band identifiers. For LTE use bands identifiers like '30' and for 5G use band identifiers like 'n30'. Maximum 256 bands per signal type.

bySignalType.description: Signal settings for the SIM. Maximum 3 signal types per SIM slot.

bySlot.description: SIMs associated with the device. Maximum 3 SIM slots per device.

post.summary: Update the cellular band masks for a device

get.description: List the clients of a device, up to a maximum of a month ago. The usage of each client is returned in kilobytes. If the device is a switch, the switchport is returned; otherwise the switchport field is null.

parameters.name: t0
parameters.description: The beginning of the timespan for the data. The maximum lookback period is 31 days from today.

parameters.name: timespan
parameters.description: The timespan for which the information will be fetched. If specifying timespan, do not specify parameter t0. The value must be in seconds and be less than or equal to 31 days. The default is 1 day.

id.description: The ID of the client

mac.description: The MAC address of the client

ip.description: The IP address of the client

vlan.description: The client-assigned name of the VLAN the client is connected to

namedVlan.description: The owner-assigned name of the VLAN the client is connected to

switchport.description: The name of the switchport with clients on it, if the device is a switch

adaptivePolicyGroup.description: A description of the adaptive policy group

usage.description: Client usage data for sent and received

get.summary: List the clients of a device, up to a maximum of a month ago

arpTableId.description: Id of the ARP table request. Used to check the status of the request.

url.description: GET this url to check the status of your ARP table request.

status.description: Status of the ARP table request.

post.description: Enqueue a job to perform a ARP table request for the device. This endpoint currently supports switches, wireless access points, and catalyst routers. This endpoint has a sustained rate limit of one request every five seconds per device, with an allowed burst of five requests.

url.description: The callback URL for the webhook target. If using this field, please also specify a sharedSecret.

sharedSecret.description: A shared secret that will be included in the requests sent to the callback URL. It can be used to verify that the request was sent by Meraki. If using this field, please also specify an url.

id.description: The webhook receiver ID that will receive information. If specifying this, please leave the url and sharedSecret fields blank.

payloadTemplate.description: The payload template of the webhook used for the callback

callback.description: Details for the callback. Please include either an httpServerId OR url and sharedSecret

get.description: Get the uplink loss percentage and latency in milliseconds, and goodput in kilobits per second for MX, MG and Z devices.

parameters.name: t0
parameters.description: The beginning of the timespan for the data. The maximum lookback period is 60 days from today.

parameters.name: t1
parameters.description: The end of the timespan for the data. t1 can be a maximum of 31 days after t0.

parameters.name: timespan
parameters.description: The timespan for which the information will be fetched. If specifying timespan, do not specify parameters t0 and t1. The value must be in seconds and be less than or equal to 31 days. The default is 1 day.

parameters.name: resolution
parameters.description: The time resolution in seconds for returned data. The valid resolutions are: 60, 600, 3600, 86400. The default is 60.

parameters.name: uplink
parameters.description: The WAN uplink used to obtain the requested stats. Valid uplinks are wan1, wan2, wan3, cellular, wan4. The default is wan1.

parameters.name: ip
parameters.description: The destination IP used to obtain the requested stats. This is required.

goodput.description: Number of useful information bits delivered
